translation.text: And I came into the garden of righteousness, and I saw many large trees growing there [their relation to the previously mentioned trees is unresolved].[a] Two of them were beautiful and great, their beauty abundant, and they were glorious; and the tree of wisdom,[b] from which those who eat know great wisdom.

footnotes.text: Not ready for application: the exact selected spatial expression and its construction remain held. The modern bracketed English label does not invent a recovered clause or silently choose among, beside or beyond from the facing Greek. The source field is provisional at this expression. The actual selected text separately has the numeral ፪ in ፪እሙ, two of them; this is not a fragrance noun and is not imported from Greek.

The singular tree of wisdom and the eating/knowing-wisdom relationship are retained. No missing tree-of-life phrase is supplied from an editor’s discussion, no numeral two is converted into two different named trees, and no complete Genesis wording is inserted.

translation.text: And it resembled [comparison unresolved][a], and its fruit was like clusters of grapes, very beautiful[b]; and the fragrance of that tree spread far away.

footnotes.text: Not ready for application: the selected comparison ሐመረ፡ ጽራእ remains meaning-unresolved in this assessment. The actual primary lexicon marks the ጽራእ term as uncertain and discusses botanical/gloss relationships; that does not establish a secure modern tree species or the full construction. The modern bracketed label is not printed Ethiopic text. The Greek height/pine-like comparison and its leaf clause are not silently substituted.

The selected fruit comparison is with vine clusters; the selected good/beautiful expression is rendered once, not doubled into both good grapes and a second separate quality. No Greek leaf-comparison clause is added to the selected Ethiopic.

translation.text: And I said, “This tree is beautiful, and how [beautiful and] delightful its appearance is!”[a]

translation.text: Then Raphael, the holy angel who was with me, answered me and said to me, “This is the tree of wisdom from which your aged father and your mother ate—your ancestors who preceded you. They knew wisdom, their eyes were opened, they knew that they were naked, and they were driven from the garden.”[a]

footnotes.text: The complete selected Ethiopic unit is printed before XXXIII. It has a singular aged father and a singular mother, followed by the plural ancestral expression አበዋቲከ፡ እለ፡ ቀደሙከ. “Your ancestors who preceded you” is a bounded, explicitly provisional apposition to those two people, not a replacement by Adam and Eve or an invented additional group. The actual longer ancestral word corrects an earlier shortened draft transcription; the primary father entry permits plural parents and forebears. The selected plural opened-eyes, knowing, nakedness and expulsion clauses remain Ethiopic text, without a supplied agent. The facing Greek gives only the short father/eating clause followed by editorial dots; it does not attest the entire Ethiopic unit, and its dots do not mark a missing Ethiopic ending. Dillmann1851 was used only as an aligned edited-Geʽez comparison, not to replace Charles’s selected word order or claim fresh manuscripts.
